projects.title: Cachiva

projects.title: MyHistory

experience.summary: Micro-frontends, API services, PostgreSQL optimization, caching, pagination and UI performance.
Enterprise Audit, ERM, ITGC and document systems with secure APIs and queue-based processing.

cachiva.problem: Technical knowledge needed to remain expressive for authors while becoming structured, searchable and dependable for readers.
constraints: One content model supports notes, nested modules, groups, bookmarks and visibility rules.
Frontend and backend require the same Markdown interpretation.
Serverless deployment requires pooled connections and predictable API contracts.
decisions: Route → controller → service → Prisma repository layers.
Zod validation, JWT authentication and standardized API envelopes.
implementation: CodeMirror authoring, drag-and-drop organization and focused reading.
PostgreSQL models for users, modules, notes, sections, bookmarks and groups.
cachiva.outcome: Structured content, access control and rendering stay synchronized across repositories.
cachiva.why: It demonstrates cross-repository contract design—not only a CRUD application—and shows how shared domain logic prevents frontend/backend drift.

discovery.problem: Multiple independently developed experiences needed to appear as one product without bundling every feature into the host.
constraints: Shared libraries cannot be duplicated across runtimes.
Every remote needs standalone development and deployment.
Remote network failures must not crash the host.
decisions: Host owns routing, state, themes and navigation.
Cosmos, Atlas and Vault expose ./App through Module Federation.
Runtime URLs are environment-configured and loaded containers are cached.
implementation: Lazy remoteEntry.js loading on route activation.
Five-attempt retries and remote-specific error boundaries.
Singleton dependency sharing for React, router, state and styling.
discovery.outcome: Three separately deployable products operate inside one consistent application shell.
discovery.why: It proves practical understanding of distributed frontend boundaries, runtime integration and failure handling—not merely static code splitting.

myhistory.problem: Private records, dated events and related spending needed one searchable system without losing original files.
constraints: File bytes stay local while metadata remains queryable.
Timelines and expenses link to supporting documents.
decisions: Filesystem stores bytes; PostgreSQL stores metadata.
Startup/resync catalog reconciles folders with database records.
Separate document, timeline and financial views connect through references.
implementation: Search, filtering, previews, downloads and collision-safe uploads.
Financial totals, category summaries and linked receipts.
myhistory.outcome: Disconnected files become searchable evidence, chronology and traceable financial records.
myhistory.why: It shows thoughtful hybrid-storage design and domain modeling while respecting the privacy boundary of sensitive personal data.
